NSF funding rates are higher then I expected--- I just looked it up as the number I heard was much lower then they say it is. (https://www.nsf.gov/funding/funding-rates.jsp?org=ENG)) But for context, I think these figures don't necessarily capture a given scientists funding likelihood. E.g. I know that scientists are (usually) clique-y and they are political (not in a right/left sense) in how they interpret the grant proposals when serving on NSF funding committees. Obviously, this effect can steer the course of a field by who is funded. Additionally, an older more well established scientist is more likely to be funded due to resources, name recognition, past contributions, etc. So the odds of getting funded end up being pretty low if you are young and in a non-sexy/hot area AND don't oversell/sensationalize your work.

Some scientists value a high standard of work and are consequentially usually well regarded. Others push/are pushed for sexy fast science and nature papers and well sometimes to be first to publish you don't know everything. This is fine, IF, you make that clear in the paper. Most good/respected authors do.

It's easy in the sense that you don't have to appeal to the person who actually earned the money at all. You might have to do significant amounts of paperwork to get the grant, but the person awarding it doesn't have to do much, and there's no real consequences if they give it to a bad project.

I suppose the taxpayer doesn't have much say/oversight on federally funded science and I have two minds on the subject.

But, these funding committees occur over the course of a week and a handful of scientists read countless proposals and try their best to evaluate them into three stacks, obviously yes, no, and maybe. Then the ones everyone voted yes and no for are piled, and then the maybes are debated. Typically these are younger researchers with less money so they have less preliminary data and their track record at doing what they propose and equipment access/ownership is more limited.

You are right, consequences for the reviewer are likely minimal, but this process utilizes a team so that can minimize a single bad/careless reviewer. However, it can lead to group think or agendas/politics. Some of these fields are quite small.
